items.stem: An app needs a private IP inside a VNet to reach an Azure Storage account so traffic never traverses the public endpoint. Which feature do you use?

options.rationale: Correct: a private endpoint projects the PaaS service into the VNet with a private IP.
A service endpoint keeps traffic on the Azure backbone but does not give the service a private IP in your VNet.
A public IP prefix allocates public addresses, the opposite of private access.
NAT gateway provides outbound SNAT; it does not privatize access to a PaaS service.

items.explanation: Correct: a private endpoint projects the PaaS service into the VNet with a private IP.

items.stem: Which gateway type is required to connect an entire on-premises site to an Azure VNet over IPsec?

options.rationale: Correct: site-to-site connects a whole on-prem network to Azure over IPsec/IKE.
Point-to-site connects individual client devices, not a whole site.
Application Gateway is a layer-7 load balancer, not a cross-premises VPN.
NAT gateway handles outbound address translation only.

items.explanation: Correct: site-to-site connects a whole on-prem network to Azure over IPsec/IKE.

items.stem: Which TWO services can filter and protect inbound HTTP/S application traffic with a Web Application Firewall policy? (Select TWO.)

options.rationale: Correct: WAF policies can be attached to Azure Front Door.
Correct: Application Gateway supports WAF policies for layer-7 protection.
Route Server exchanges BGP routes; it does not run a WAF.
An NSG filters by IP/port, not by HTTP inspection with a WAF ruleset.
Bastion provides secure RDP/SSH, not web application firewalling.

items.explanation: Correct: WAF policies can be attached to Azure Front Door. Correct: Application Gateway supports WAF policies for layer-7 protection.
